children: Venture capitalist Joe Lonsdale is advising investors to avoid bonds for the next decade and focus instead on equities, arguing that surging demand for artificial intelligence will drive higher interest rates and make fixed income a losing bet.
co-founder made the case during an interview with CNBC following his appearance at the Venture Dallas conference.

"I do not think you want to own bonds for the next 10 years because there's going to be a higher demand for money," Lonsdale said. "There's going to be higher interest rates. That means bonds will not do as well in the next ten years."

He recommended that investors stay long in the stock market to capture productivity gains from the AI revolution, specifically favoring companies with technical talent and processes positioned to become more efficient.

Lonsdale painted a picture of rapidly accelerating AI adoption, noting that the pace of development has become extraordinary. He pointed to startups with just 10 employees now leveraging the equivalent of 800 virtual agents to build products at unprecedented speed.
The demand for AI compute and infrastructure is scaling dramatically, according to Lonsdale.
He projected AI-related revenue will reach a few hundred billion dollars this year, climb toward $1T next year, and hit $2T the year after that.
"So, there's a huge demand for infrastructure and compute," he said.
For everyday investors looking to participate in the AI-driven wealth creation, Lonsdale offered straightforward advice.
"I think the least risky way is to be long in the stock market…to be long in the economy. Productivity is going up," he said.
He specifically endorsed investing in the S&P 500 (
) as "a great thing to do" while cautioning investors to be "very careful" with fixed income holdings.

title: Investors should not own bonds for the next 10 years – Palantir co-founder Joe Lonsdale
